messages:
devon: seeing repeated OOMs and container restarts on gpu-pool-7 over the last 30m. node flapping, pods in CrashLoopBackOff. stack: paged-attention allocator hitting fragmentation, KV cache growth steady. logs:
```
E/CUDA: 0x7f9b2c - CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
runtime: alloc failed: allocator=PagedAttention::alloc size=1.2G
kvcache: resident_pages=1.1G, free_pages=80M, fragmentation_ratio=0.74
containerd: container 'serving/runtime-abc' exited code=137
```
Any quick wins before we escalate?

maria: on it. I'm rolling up logs + correlating with recent deploys. Initial guess: attention paging thresholds + KV cache compaction not keeping up with long-tail sequences from batch jobs. Noting increased request spike from /api/chat - looks like a user-simulated load test at ~09:12 UTC.

incident-bot: Incident created: SEV2 - gpu-pool-7 OOMs & node flaps. Paging & kvcache suspected. Bridge: https://redwood.inc/bridge/INC-620-7 :bell:
Tags: oncall, eng-runtime, eng-sre

samir: do we have an immediate mitigation? can we force fallback to the non-paged runtime? runtime flag exists: --attention-paging=off (will raise memory use per-request but reduces allocator fragmentation).

maria: good call. I recommend:
1) set `ATTN_PAGING=off` on pool gpu-pool-7 (hotfix) on the pod template
2) increase kvcache eviction aggressiveness: `KV_EVICT_THRESHOLD=0.6` -> `0.4`
3) scale pool + cordon busiest node to drain
I'll push a change to staging and roll to one node as canary.

devon: doing (1) on a single canary pod now. command:
```
kubectl patch deployment runtime-serving -n inference --type='json' -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/env/ATTN_PAGING","value":"off"}]'
```
watching logs.

deploy-bot: rolling update started for deployment/runtime-serving in inference (canary). image: runtime:v4.2.1-hotfix

maria: canary pod came up clean. memory use jumped ~300MB per-request but allocator fragmentation stopped increasing. No immediate OOM on the canary.

devon: observed one pod restart on node gpu-7b during the change, but it stayed healthy after restart. CUDA errors subsided on the canary.

samir: recommend also enabling the nightly kvcache-sweeper task sooner: run `scripts/kvcache_sweep.py --max-runtime 10m --aggressive` on affected pool to compact pages. I'll kick it now.

```
./scripts/kvcache_sweep.py --pool gpu-pool-7 --aggressive
```

ops-bot: kvcache_sweep invoked by samir on gpu-pool-7 (run id: sweep-620-01). Estimated run: ~8m.

maria: customer impact note: ~4% of /api/chat requests returned 502 during the 09:05-09:20 window; latency for successful requests increased median +120ms. Affected tenants: client-alpha (high), internal-load-tests (very high). No data loss. We routed some traffic to the fallback model `small-1` which increased token spend but kept sessions alive.

ashley: are any SLA targets breached? Do we need to notify growth/SRE?

maria: not yet SLA-breach level, but customer-alpha had degraded experience. I'm drafting a short customer notification for the status page with note about degraded latency and mitigation steps.

devon: after sweeper finished, fragmentation ratio dropped to 0.31 and resident pages settled. Still monitoring KV growth over the next hour.

samir: longer-term: we should land a runtime change to improve page compaction during steady-state (auto-compact on low-util windows), and add telemetry alerts for fragmentation_ratio > 0.6. I'll create a tracker ticket.

maria: created GH issue: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/issues/3215 - will include logs, canary results, and the recommended runtime flags.

devon: for oncall handoff: summary for next shift:
- root cause: paged-attention allocator fragmentation + slow KV cache growth due to long-tail sequences + one traffic spike from load-test
- immediate mitigations applied: attention paging disabled on affected pool, aggressive kvcache sweep, scaled pool + drained flapping node
- customer impact: transient 502s (~4%), increased latency. traffic routed to fallback small-1 while mitigations landed
- next actions: monitor KV resident_pages for 2hr, revert to paging=on only after fragmentation_ratio < 0.4 for 30m, track follow-up GH issue
- links: bridge, sweep run id sweep-620-01, GH #3215

Please pick up monitoring and escalate if OOMs reappear.

ashley: taking handoff. will watch for 2hrs, coordinate with samir if ratio climbs. also will notify growth ops if client-alpha reports. :thumbsup:

maria: handing off detailed runbook notes to @ashley in the incident doc (docs/redwood-runbooks/kvcache-paged-oom.md). Leaving cluster-level logs attached to the GH issue. Good work team. :raised_hands:
